docs.title: Stellwerk
docs.text:
Central web UI to manage Syncthing on all your devices. A small agent on each device brings its own Syncthing and keeps it at the state the server sets; a hub Syncthing on the server is a member of every folder.

Stellwerk is in early development; see Architecture for the design and the roadmap.

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
• Zentrale (crates/zentrale): one Rust binary with login, SQLite, the desired state of every device with a revision number, the connections to all agents, and the web UI.
  • Hub Syncthing on the server: steered by the Zentrale with the same code as the devices, member of every folder, keeps versions.
  • Agent (crates/agent) on every device: starts its own Syncthing, brings its configuration to the desired state, reports status.
  • protocol: the messages and the desired state. Describes devices, folders, modes and paths only.
  • engine: the only crate that knows Syncthing.

The Zentrale never sends commands like "create folder X", always "this is how it should look, revision 42". Applying is idempotent, so a device that was offline simply gets the current state.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
The agent opens a WebSocket to the Zentrale (/api/agent/ws); messages are JSON with a type field (crates/protocol/src/messages.rs).

Direction Message Content Zentrale → agent challenge a fresh nonce agent → Zentrale hello public key, signature over the nonce, on first contact the one-time code; host name, OS, agent and Syncthing version, Syncthing device ID, last applied revision Zentrale → agent welcome the device's ID at the Zentrale Zentrale → agent desiredState revision, peers (device IDs and addresses), folders with ID, label, mode, path, versioning, ignore patterns, peers agent → Zentrale applied revision, errors per folder agent → Zentrale status per folder: state, files and bytes in total and still needed, errors; on change, at most about once per second Zentrale → agent rejected why; the socket closes

The desired state is always complete, never a diff: an agent that was offline for three days just gets the current state when it connects.

docs.title: Pairing
docs.text:
1. "Pair device" in the UI: the Zentrale creates a one-time code (valid for 15 minutes) and stores only its hash.
  2. On the device: stellwerk-agent join --server https://… <code> creates an Ed25519 key and stores server, key and code; stellwerk-agent run starts the agent.
  3. The agent answers the Zentrale's challenge with a hello signed by its key and carrying the code. The Zentrale uses the code up and creates the device; the agent drops the code.
  4. From then on the agent signs in with its key only. A blocked device is turned away.

The hub Syncthing listens on its own port (22001 by default, --hub-listen), so a Syncthing already running on the server keeps 22000. Devices dial the hub at --hub-address; the hub never needs to reach the devices.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
SQLite with migrations embedded in the binary (crates/zentrale/migrations).

Table Columns devices id, name, kind, os, public_key, syncthing_id, agent_version, syncthing_version, approved, created_at, last_seen, applied_rev folders id, label, syncthing_folder_id, ignore_patterns, versioning, encrypted_on_hub, created_at shares folder_id, device_id, mode, path (no row = "off") enrollments code_hash, expires_at, used_at, device_id config_rev one revision number, raised in the same transaction as every change events at, device, folder, kind, text (activity feed) admin, sessions login

docs.title: Login and API
docs.text:
One admin with a password (argon2id), set with stellwerk set-password on the server. A login sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie (Secure behind HTTPS) and returns a CSRF token the UI sends back in X-CSRF-Token on every change. Only hashes of session tokens and pairing codes are stored.

Endpoint Does GET /api/session, POST /api/login, POST /api/logout login state, log in, log out GET /api/overview revision, hub, devices (with online state), folders, shares POST /api/folders, PATCH/DELETE /api/folders/{id} create, rename, remove a folder POST /api/shares apply a matrix draft as one revision PATCH/DELETE /api/devices/{id} rename, block, remove a device POST /api/enrollments, POST /api/enrollments/status new pairing code, has a device used it yet GET /api/events activity feed

Every change raises the revision and sends connected agents and the hub their new desired state.

docs.title: Desired states
docs.text:
crates/zentrale/src/desired.rs turns the stored configuration into one desired state per device and one for the hub, as pure functions. The topology is a star:

  • a device has the hub as its only peer and shares each of its folders with the hub;
  • the hub has every approved device as a peer and holds every folder under <data>/folders/<syncthing folder id>, in mode "both", with staggered versioning (one year by default), shared with every device that has the folder;
  • a blocked device gets no desired state and disappears from the hub's peers and folders.

docs.title: Web UI
docs.text:
web/: React with TanStack Router (file-based routes), Query and Table, Tailwind 4 with design tokens for light and dark, components in shadcn style on Radix, lucide icons. The release build of the Zentrale embeds web/dist; paths outside /api fall back to index.html.

  • Übersicht: devices online, folders, revision; the folder × device matrix. Clicks collect in a draft ("3 ungespeicherte Änderungen") and "Anwenden" sends it as one revision. The server column is fixed: the hub holds every folder. Cells of an offline device that has not applied the current revision show "wartet".
  • Geräte: list with search and filter, rename, block, remove; "Gerät koppeln" creates a code, shows the command per OS and waits until the device shows up, then asks for its name and folders.
  • Ordner: mode and local path per device; versions per file with restore; conflicts side by side; rename, ignore patterns (one per line, on every device and the hub), remove.
  • Konflikte: every conflict of every folder in one list.

German and English with Paraglide: messages in web/messages/{de,en}.json, compiled to typed functions; the language follows the browser and can be switched in the sidebar (kept in local storage).

Live updates come through /api/ws (see above); polling every 30 seconds is only the fallback. src/api/types.ts checks every answer with Zod. pnpm dev:demo runs the UI on fixtures (src/demo/) without a Zentrale. The Playwright tests in e2e/ and the screenshots (pnpm screenshots, or Actions → Update screenshots) use the same demo mode, so they need neither Rust nor Syncthing.

docs.title: Live status and activity
docs.text:
The engine's monitor (crates/engine/src/monitor.rs) long-polls Syncthing's /rest/events and reads /rest/db/status for every folder whenever something happened, at most once per second.

  • Each agent sends the result as status over its WebSocket.
  • The Zentrale watches the hub the same way and also reads /rest/db/completion for every folder and device: how much of a folder a device has, known from its index even while it is offline ("214 changes wait on the server").
  • Changes that arrive at the hub (RemoteChangeDetected, with the short ID of the device that made them) are counted per device and folder over 30 seconds and written to the activity feed ("laptop changed 18 files in Projekte"), as are pairings, connects and disconnects.
  • The UI gets everything through /api/ws: one update with revision, online devices and the live state per change (throttled to 300 ms). The status goes straight into the query cache; a new revision or online state reloads the overview.

Syncthing keeps events for a mask only from its first request on (lib/api/api.go, getEventSub), so the monitor starts together with Syncthing.

docs.title: Conflicts and versions
docs.text:
The hub holds every folder in full, so both are handled there and Syncthing carries the result to every device (crates/engine/src/files.rs, crates/zentrale/src/files.rs).

  • Conflicts. Syncthing names a conflict copy name.sync-conflict-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<short ID>.ext (lib/model/folder_sendrecv.go). The Zentrale searches the hub's folders every 30 seconds, notes new conflicts in the activity feed and shows both sides, with a line diff for text up to 256 KB. Resolving happens on the hub's disk, followed by a rescan:
  • keep the current file: the copy goes to the versions;
  • keep the copy: the current file goes to the versions, the copy takes its name;
  • keep both: the copy becomes name.<device>.ext next to the original.

The discarded side is moved into .stversions under Syncthing's own naming (name~YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.ext, lib/versioner/util.go), so it shows up among the versions. The time in that name is UTC; Syncthing reads it as local time, which is the same in the Docker image. - Versions. The hub keeps staggered versions (a year by default). The UI lists them through GET /rest/folder/versions and restores one with POST /rest/folder/versions, which archives the current file first.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text: Module Does pin the pinned Syncthing version and the SHA-256 of each platform's release archive download fetches the archive once into a cache directory, checks it, unpacks binary and license process starts Syncthing with its own --home, GUI/API on 127.0.0.1 with a random port and a fresh API key; no auto-upgrade, no usage reporting client Syncthing REST API: /rest/config, /rest/config/{devices,folders}/{id}, /rest/db/scan, … reconcile pure function: actual config + desired state → list of API calls apply runs those calls; the only side effects of reconciling monitor event stream, folder status, completion of other devices, changes that arrived files conflict copies and versions in a folder on disk: find, parse, resolve, archive

docs.title: Reconciler
docs.text:
1. Read GET /rest/config and the own device ID.
  2. Compare with the desired state: add missing devices and folders, change differing ones, remove those no longer wanted. The own device is never removed.
  3. Write the changes with PUT/DELETE on /rest/config/devices/{id} and /rest/config/folders/{id}, devices before the folders that name them; then the ignore patterns with POST /rest/db/ignores?folder={id} where they differ from GET (empty lines and trailing spaces do not count).

A folder with a new path is removed and added again, so Syncthing starts with a fresh index instead of treating the files at the old path as deleted. The reconciler only changes configuration; removing a folder leaves its files alone.

Mode Syncthing folder type Both sendreceive Send only sendonly Receive only receiveonly Off folder not present on the device

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Phase Content Gate 0 · Spike ✅ engine starts Syncthing, reconciler applies a fixed desired state integration test "file from A arrives on B" is green 1 · MVP ✅ Zentrale with SQLite, agent over WebSocket, pairing with a one-time code, hub Syncthing, matrix and device list in the UI 3-node test with an offline device green (crates/zentrale/tests/phase1_gate.rs), own devices one week in daily use (open) 2 · Comfort ✅ live status, activity, conflicts on the hub, versions, ignore patterns, German and English E2E green, conflict and restore in the integration test (crates/zentrale/tests/phase2_gate.rs) 3 · Distribution installers, LAN discovery, self-update with signature, Docker image and Quadlet v1.0 published through release.yml

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The Zentrale runs as a container (Docker or Podman) or as a single binary; the agent is a single binary per device. Until v1.0 is released, build the image and the binaries from source; from v1.0 on the image is tristanteu/stellwerk on Docker Hub and ghcr.io/firsttris/stellwerk.

docs.title: Zentrale as a container
docs.text: The image holds the Zentrale with the UI and the pinned Syncthing, runs as an unprivileged user and keeps everything under /data. Build it locally with docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t stellwerk ..

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
services:
  stellwerk:
    image: tristanteu/stellwerk:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"   # web UI and agents, behind a TLS proxy
      - "22001:22001"           # sync port of the hub, reachable from the devices
    environment:
      STELLWERK_HUB_ADDRESS: tcp://sync.example.org:22001
    volumes:
      - stellwerk:/data
volumes:
  stellwerk:

docker compose up -d
docker compose exec -T stellwerk stellwerk set-password <<< 'a long password'

docs.title: Podman Quadlet
docs.text:
/etc/containers/systemd/stellwerk.container:

[Unit]
Description=Stellwerk Zentrale

[Container]
Image=docker.io/tristanteu/stellwerk:latest
PublishPort=127.0.0.1:8080:8080
PublishPort=22001:22001
Environment=STELLWERK_HUB_ADDRESS=tcp://sync.example.org:22001
Volume=stellwerk.volume:/data
AutoUpdate=registry

[Service]
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

/etc/containers/systemd/stellwerk.volume holds only [Volume]. Then:

systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl start stellwerk
podman exec -i systemd-stellwerk stellwerk set-password <<< 'a long password'

Set STELLWERK_HUB_ADDRESS in either case: inside a container the host name is the container's. The container stops cleanly on SIGTERM; the hub Syncthing is shut down with it.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Requires Rust (stable), Node 22 and pnpm.

git clone https://github.com/firsttris/stellwerk && cd stellwerk
pnpm install && pnpm --filter web build      # the UI, embedded into the Zentrale
cargo build --release                        # target/release/stellwerk and stellwerk-agent

docs.title: Zentrale as a binary
docs.text:
stellwerk --data-dir /srv/stellwerk set-password      # once; reads the password from stdin
stellwerk --data-dir /srv/stellwerk \
  --listen 0.0.0.0:8080 \
  --hub-listen tcp://0.0.0.0:22001 \
  --hub-address tcp://sync.example.org:22001
Option Default --data-dir (STELLWERK_DATA) data database, hub Syncthing and the hub's copy of every folder --listen (STELLWERK_LISTEN) 0.0.0.0:8080 web UI and the agents' WebSocket; put it behind a TLS proxy such as Caddy --hub-listen (STELLWERK_HUB_LISTEN) tcp://0.0.0.0:22001 sync port of the hub; not 22000, so a Syncthing already running keeps its port --hub-address (STELLWERK_HUB_ADDRESS) host name + hub port where devices reach the hub --syncthing (STELLWERK_SYNCTHING) download a Syncthing binary instead of the pinned release

The hub port must be reachable from the devices; the web port only through the proxy.

docs.title: Agent on a device
docs.text:
In the UI, Gerät koppeln shows the command with a one-time code:

stellwerk-agent join --server https://sync.example.org K7Q2-MX9P-41TZ
stellwerk-agent run

The agent keeps its key, its own Syncthing and Syncthing's database in its data directory (~/.local/share/stellwerk-agent on Linux, --data-dir to change it). It downloads the pinned Syncthing on first start and never touches a Syncthing that is already installed. Running it as a service (systemd, Windows service, launchd) comes with the installers in phase 3.
